newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Hard-up Kazakh causes panic with chlorine hoax.
newsitem.headline: Hard-up Kazakh causes panic with chlorine hoax.

text.p: A man protesting over unpaid wages almost forced large-scale evacuations in a major industrial town in Kazakhstan when he left a dummy bomb attached to a 50-tonne cistern containing chlorine, a newspaper said on Thursday.
the official Kazakhstanskaya Pravda daily said the dummy bomb was found stuck to a cistern in the north-eastern town of Pavlodar along with a note saying: "Pay me my salary!"

Authorities, fearing the release of poisonous chlorine gas, evacuated workers of a nearby chemical plant and were making emergency evacuation plans for the entire city of 400,000, when the bomb was discovered to be a dummy.
The newspaper did not say when the incident occurred. The man has not been found.

Kazakhstan faces a huge backlog of unpaid salaries and pensions reaching 60 billion tenge ($792 million). President Nursultan Nazarbayev has threatened to sack all government and regional officials unable to improve the situation by April 1.
